checks: Each cap formula has negative section flux on a proper cut because its new outer normal is -v_j. At an inside supporting face the old normal is -v_j and the body and section coefficients sum to one. At an outside support the normal is v_j and the coefficients cancel. Lower-dimensional supporting contacts contribute zero area, while d=1 correctly uses endpoint counting.

The full-body identity minus the weighted cap identities produces a positive raw section term. With X(x)=x and multiplier p this is the integral of p(b_j-a_j·p). The common centroid expansion leaves S_j p̄_i(b_j-a_j·p̄_i) minus V_j^{pp}a_j. The first pieces cancel under the exact group balance.

The support label normal equals both actual boundary marks. Its constant plane term integrates to zero against W_θ, and the p-weighted height term gives the negative body pp covariance. The bounded fields and finite measures justify the label integral. Repeating for X(x)=x(h·x), with divergence (d+1)h·x, gives the two negative transposed px terms, converted by the two kernel identities into positive xx terms. At zero base dimension each xx-normal product vanishes.

The rectangle check uses three unit-length intervals. At the center closed nonvertical cuts through it have mass 3/2 by symmetry and null boundaries, and pure-base cuts contain at least two fibers. Horizontal cuts bound all marks above by 3/2. Exact rational integration gives p-cap moments (1/2,0), x-cap moments (5/16,-3/8), pp section moments (2,2), and xx section moments (1/8,0). Identity boundary coupling gives Q_θ=0, hence the two residuals are -1/2 and 1/8. The support statuses and both signs match the three original locators.
